cards.title: Auto Chips Market Heading to $160B by 2031

panels.head: Automotive chips are on track to double in six years
panels.sub: Yole Group pegs the automotive semiconductor market at $77B today and forecasts it hits $160B by 2031 — a ~13% CAGR sustained across a full product cycle.

panels.head: Four forces, not one
panels.sub: Electrification, ADAS sensor fusion, centralised compute architectures, and software-defined vehicle platforms are each independently pulling chip spend upward — making the trend broad rather than fragile.

panels.head: Zonal and domain controllers are replacing ECU sprawl
panels.sub: Centralised compute means fewer but far more powerful SoCs per vehicle. That concentrates silicon value — and perception pipeline workloads — into a handful of high-ASP chips rather than dozens of microcontrollers.

panels.head: Computer vision sits at the core of every ADAS dollar
panels.sub: Camera, radar, and LiDAR fusion is the primary workload on centralised ADAS SoCs. PMs building CV inference pipelines for automotive have a six-year tailwind; the constraint will be safety certification speed, not hardware availability.

panels.head: Follow the architecture, not the headline number
panels.sub: The shift to software-defined vehicles means OTA-updatable perception stacks. That creates a recurring software revenue opportunity layered on top of the hardware growth — worth tracking separately from the chip market itself.

cards.title: One-shotting a browser game with Claude Fable 5

panels.head: A 2022 tweet became a playable 3D browser game — no design decisions made by the human
panels.sub: Simon Willison fed Claude Fable 5 two screenshots from a 2022 GPT-3/DALL-E concept tweet and a single mobile-typed prompt. He made zero further choices. A working raccoon heist game came out the other end.

panels.head: GitHub Pages as a live preview loop for Claude Code sessions
panels.sub: Claude Code for web can't easily serve a preview mid-session. The workaround: point GitHub Pages at Claude's auto-named branch. Every push is live within ~30 seconds, giving you a real URL to watch the build progress in real time.

panels.head: The prompt delegated everything: stack, art style, game mechanics
panels.sub: Willison told Fable 5 to use an OpenAI API key for procedural textures (gpt-image-2), stay mobile-friendly, commit often, and log its own decisions to notes.md. He assumed — correctly — it would reach for Three.js unprompted.

panels.head: The real unlock is autonomous iteration, not just code generation
panels.sub: Fable 5 didn't need hand-holding between commits. It generated assets, structured the game loop, and self-documented its choices. The human's role was environment setup (repo + Pages config) and spec-writing — about 15 minutes of work.

panels.head: For PMs: treat the model as a solo contractor, not a copilot
panels.sub: The prompt pattern — give assets, set constraints, forbid interruptions, demand frequent deploys — maps directly to how you'd brief a freelancer. The GitHub Pages loop is the key missing piece for async verification without blocking the agent.

cards.title: Accidental button presses kill streaming sessions

panels.head: You sit on the remote. The movie disappears.
panels.sub: Accidental button presses on TV remotes kick users out of streaming apps mid-watch — a small but recurring frustration in every household with a couch.

panels.head: Anyone who shares a sofa owns this problem
panels.sub: Families with kids, older users unfamiliar with deep app navigation, and anyone watching in the dark. The annoyance scales with how many steps it takes to return to the same point in content.

panels.head: A soft-lock layer for streaming remotes — or the apps themselves
panels.sub: Hardware path: a hold-to-activate lock mode on physical remotes. Software path: a streaming app setting that requires a deliberate double-press or hold before exiting playback. The software route could ship without any OEM involvement.

panels.head: Nothing solves this today
panels.sub: Remote cases and couch organisers prevent loss, not accidental presses. Streaming apps offer no exit confirmation or lock mode. Smart TV OS vendors (Roku, FireTV, Google TV) haven't shipped this as a system-level feature.

panels.head: Search before you build
panels.sub: Check r/Roku, r/fireTV, and r/cordcutters for duplicate complaints — volume and recency will tell you whether this is a top-10 pain point or background noise. If it surfaces often, a browser extension or Android TV sideload app is a low-cost first test.

cards.title: LLM 0.32: reasoning traces, server tools, smarter logs

panels.head: Your CLI can now watch a model think — and keep it out of your pipes
panels.sub: LLM 0.32 streams reasoning traces to stderr, so a model's chain-of-thought is visible on screen but never pollutes stdout when you're chaining commands.

panels.head: Server-side tools land in one flag
panels.cmd: llm --tool CodeInterpreter 'Show current python and SQLite versions'
panels.sub: OpenAI's sandboxed code executor and web search are now callable directly from the CLI. The llm-anthropic plugin adds WebSearch, WebFetch, CodeExecution, and MCP server access in the same pattern.

panels.head: One-liner to hit any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — no install needed
panels.cmd: uvx --with llm-tools-quickjs llm openai endpoint http://localhost:1234/v1 -m google/gemma-4-12b -T QuickJS 'Use QuickJS to multiply 3434 * 2434' --td
panels.sub: The new `llm openai endpoint` command runs a prompt against any compatible API (local LM Studio, remote self-hosted, etc.) as a one-shot. These calls are intentionally not logged.

panels.head: The Python API now maps to how LLMs actually work
panels.sub: Instead of a fake conversation abstraction, you can pass a raw message list with system/user/assistant turns. Streaming now emits typed events — 'reasoning', 'text', tool calls, image attachments — so your code handles the real response shape rather than assuming a flat string.

panels.head: Default model quietly upgrades to GPT-5.6 Luna
panels.sub: A bare `llm "prompt"` now routes to GPT-5.6 Luna — cheap, capable, and the new baseline. If you're building pipelines or evals on top of the LLM CLI, audit your default-model assumptions before upgrading.

cards.title: llm-anthropic 0.26: Claude 5 + server tools
cards.headline:
Claude 5 models, built-in
web search, and smarter
thinking controls

steps.label: Three new Claude 5 models
steps.detail: claude-fable-5, claude-sonnet-5, and claude-opus-5 are now available. Fable 5 always reasons; Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 reason by default but you can disable it.

steps.label: Server-side tools via -T flag
steps.detail: WebSearch, WebFetch, CodeExecution, and AnthropicMCP are now first-class tools. The old -o web_search* options are gone — switch to -T WebSearch.

steps.label: Simplified thinking controls
steps.detail: Extended thinking collapses to two options: thinking (on/off) and thinking_effort (low/medium/high/xhigh/max). The old thinking_budget and thinking_adaptive knobs are removed.

steps.label: Hide reasoning from output
steps.detail: Pass --hide-reasoning / -R to suppress chain-of-thought from stdout and logs. Without it, reasoning streams to stderr so it doesn't pollute piped output.

steps.label: Typed streaming events (LLM 0.32)
steps.detail: Reasoning, tool calls, and tool results now stream as distinct typed events, making it easier to parse or display intermediate steps in scripts and UIs.

cards.title: Neuraspace raises $18M for European space traffic management

panels.head: Europe wants its own eyes on what's orbiting overhead
panels.sub: Portuguese startup Neuraspace closed ~$18M in fresh funding on Aug. 5, targeting sovereign space domain awareness — the ability to track objects in orbit without relying on US Space Command data feeds.

panels.head: Space traffic management is a dependency problem
panels.sub: Most commercial and government operators today lean on US SSN (Space Surveillance Network) for conjunction alerts. As LEO congestion grows — Starlink alone exceeds 6,000 satellites — European agencies want an independent picture they control.

panels.head: AI-driven collision risk, not just raw tracking
panels.sub: Neuraspace layers machine learning on top of sensor data to produce actionable manoeuvre recommendations, moving the product from 'here are the objects' to 'here is what to do about them'. The $18M is earmarked to expand sensor network partnerships and defense-facing capabilities.

panels.head: Defence funding is reshaping the space awareness market
panels.sub: The explicit mention of 'defense capabilities' signals military procurement interest — European NATO members are prioritising space situational awareness as a strategic asset, opening a government-contract revenue lane alongside commercial satellite operators.

panels.head: Sovereign SDA is a platform play, not just a service
panels.sub: Whoever owns the authoritative collision-risk data feed for European operators gains leverage over the entire stack: insurance underwriting, spectrum coordination, and eventual regulatory compliance. Watch for Neuraspace to pursue ESA and national-agency anchor contracts next.

cards.title: Space Force awards $615M for airborne-target tracking sats

panels.head: $615M to watch the sky from space
panels.sub: The U.S. Space Force has awarded contracts totalling $615 million across Rocket Lab, STR, and one undisclosed vendor for its Airborne Moving Target Indication (AMTI) satellite program.

panels.head: AMTI: tracking airborne threats from orbit
panels.sub: AMTI satellites are designed to detect and track moving airborne objects — aircraft, missiles, drones — from low Earth orbit, filling a gap that ground and airborne radar systems can't cover globally.

panels.head: Rocket Lab diversifies beyond launch — again
panels.sub: STR is a defence-focused space sensing firm; Rocket Lab's win extends its growing spacecraft and systems business, which now competes separately from its Electron and Neutron launch vehicles.

panels.head: Space-based wide-area surveillance is scaling fast
panels.sub: Multiple vendors on a single programme signals the Space Force is pursuing resilience through competition rather than a single-contractor constellation — a pattern accelerating across its Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture.

panels.head: Defence is the near-term revenue floor for LEO sensing
panels.sub: For commercial CV and edge-compute players, AMTI-class programmes validate the sensor-to-orbit pipeline. The technology overlap with commercial Earth observation — onboard processing, moving-object detection — is direct.
